identity.title: Overparametrization bends the landscape: BBP transitions at initialization in simple Neural Networks

problem.claim: Analyze how overparameterization affects the loss landscape and initialization informativeness in a simple teacher–student learning problem generalizing phase retrieval.

contributions.claim: A field-theoretic Hessian-spectrum analysis identifies a BBP data transition separating informative and uninformative initialization regimes.

The analysis shows that overparameterization shifts the transition, potentially reaching the information-theoretic weak-recovery threshold at large overparameterization, while changing whether the transition is continuous or discontinuous.
For discontinuous transitions, the authors estimate a lower SNR threshold below which initialization becomes entirely uninformative.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors emphasize that overparameterization can bend the landscape by shifting and qualitatively altering BBP transitions, including their limiting location and continuity type.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report simulations supporting their analytical predictions and compare them with finite-N behavior.
For discontinuous BBP transitions, the authors report that strong finite-N corrections permit information retrieval at an SNR below the predicted BBP transition.
The authors report estimates of a new lower SNR threshold marking when initialization becomes entirely uninformative in those discontinuous-transition cases.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper frames high-dimensional non-convex landscapes and their interaction with gradient-based optimization as an important question, even in simple models.
It studies a prototypical teacher–student problem that generalizes phase retrieval to overparameterized settings.
Using field-theory techniques, it analyzes the initialization Hessian spectrum and identifies informative versus uninformative BBP regimes.
It reports that overparameterization shifts the transition toward the weak-recovery threshold and can change its continuous or discontinuous character.
For discontinuous transitions, finite-N corrections are reported to enable lower-SNR retrieval and motivate a lower uninformative threshold.

source_observation.claim: The abstract separates the asymptotic BBP transition from finite-N corrections and introduces a distinct lower SNR threshold for complete loss of initialization information.

lessons.interpretation: This preserves the distinction between a predicted phase boundary and finite-size operational behavior.
lessons.application: When presenting phase-transition results, report the asymptotic boundary, finite-size deviations, and any separately defined practical threshold as different quantities.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the study has no finite-size analysis or no operationally distinct threshold.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the exact model, scaling, signal-to-noise parametrization, or overparameterization limit.
Simulation sizes, quantitative threshold estimates, and the extent of agreement with finite-N behavior are not given.
The abstract does not provide details sufficient to assess the analytical derivation or the meaning of “entirely uninformative.”
